title: Claude Fable 5 & Mythos 5: The Mythos-Class Tier
content:
## Overview

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic introduced **Mythos-class** — a new capability tier that sits above Opus — and released two models built on it: **Claude Fable 5**, generally available to the public, and **Claude Mythos 5**, restricted to vetted partners. Anthropic describes Fable 5's capabilities as exceeding any model it has previously made generally available, with especially strong results in software engineering, knowledge work, vision, and scientific research.

Before this release, Mythos-class access was limited to cyber-defense partners and a handful of biology researchers under a "Mythos Preview" program. Fable 5 is the first Mythos-class model opened to the general public.

---

## One Model, Two Safeguard Configurations

Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are **the same underlying model** — the difference is a safeguard layer. Fable 5 ships with classifiers that intercept requests in three sensitive domains and silently reroute them to Claude Opus 4.8 instead of answering with the more capable model:

- Cybersecurity (offensive tooling, exploit development)
- Biology and chemistry (dual-use research of concern)
- Model distillation (extracting another model's weights/behavior via API)

Because of this routing, **Fable 5 only exhibits Mythos-class performance outside those safeguarded domains** — inside them, a Fable 5 API call is effectively answered by Opus 4.8.

Claude Mythos 5 is Fable 5 with the cybersecurity safeguard lifted, made available to organizations Anthropic has vetted. It is not accessible through standard API accounts.

---

## Claude Fable 5 Specs

| Spec | Value |
|---|---|
| Context window | 1,000,000 tokens (text, image, file input) |
| Max output | 128K tokens |
| Thinking | Always-on adaptive thinking |
| API model ID | `claude-fable-5` |
| Pricing | $10 / $50 per million input/output tokens |

**Benchmarks** (per Anthropic and third-party evaluators):
- SWE-Bench Verified: 95.0% (vs. Opus 4.8's 88.6%, GPT-5.5's 82.6%)
- SWE-Bench Pro: 80.3% (vs. GPT-5.5's 58.6%)
- Leads on nearly every benchmark Anthropic published at launch

Fable 5's list price is double Opus 4.8's, but less than half of what the earlier Mythos Preview cost. Through June 22, 2026, it was included at no extra charge on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans; after that date, using it requires usage credits at standard API rates.

---

## Claude Mythos 5 and Project Glasswing

Mythos 5 is initially being deployed through **Project Glasswing**, a collaboration with the US government, as an upgrade to the earlier Mythos Preview. Anthropic describes it as having the strongest cybersecurity capabilities of any model in the world. US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stated he had "determined that appropriate safeguards are in place to permit certain trusted partners to access the Claude Mythos 5 Model," following talks between the government and Anthropic.

Access is limited to roughly 150 vetted organizations at launch — cyber-defense partners first, with select biology researchers (biology/chemistry safeguards lifted) expected to follow, pending Anthropic's broader trusted-access program.

**Security note:** Shortly after launch, reporting surfaced that unauthorized third parties had gained access to a restricted Mythos deployment through a combination of process failures, reportedly informed by knowledge from an unrelated data breach. This is a reminder that Mythos-class access controls — not just model capability — are part of what's being evaluated as this tier matures.

---

## Why It Matters

Mythos-class is the first time Anthropic has formalized a capability tier *above* Opus, and the first time it has shipped a model whose full capability is deliberately withheld from the general public via safeguard routing rather than simply not being released. It signals two things: frontier capability is advancing fast enough that Anthropic feels it needs an extra safety tier, and government coordination (via programs like Project Glasswing) is now a formal part of how the most capable models reach the field.
